judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 1084. The Dismantling DEI Departments Act bars state and local governments and public colleges from diversity, equity, or inclusion preferences and offices, and cancels conflicting policies. Exceptions protect federal funding, demographic public-health and medical work, disease prevention, and equal outreach without quotas or preferences. The Tennessee House passed it 72-25, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 1084. The Dismantling DEI Departments Act bars state and local governments and public colleges from diversity, equity, or inclusion preferences and offices, and cancels conflicting policies. Exceptions protect federal funding, demographic public-health and medical work, disease prevention, and equal outreach without quotas or preferences. The Tennessee House passed it 72-25, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 1713. Starting January 1, 2027, leaders of state and local governments and public colleges must certify yearly to the comptroller that they used no diversity, equity, or inclusion preference. The attorney general may investigate claims that a state office broke the ban. The Tennessee House passed it 66-20, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 1713. Starting January 1, 2027, leaders of state and local governments and public colleges must certify yearly to the comptroller that they used no diversity, equity, or inclusion preference. The attorney general may investigate claims that a state office broke the ban. The Tennessee House passed it 66-20, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 749. Tennessee rejects an out-of-state license issued only to people illegally in the country when its markings differ from licenses for citizens and legal residents; driving with one is a Class B misdemeanor, a lower-level crime. The safety department must publish and keep a list of these license types by December 1, 2025. The Tennessee House passed it 68-21, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against House Bill 749. Tennessee rejects an out-of-state license issued only to people illegally in the country when its markings differ from licenses for citizens and legal residents; driving with one is a Class B misdemeanor, a lower-level crime. The safety department must publish and keep a list of these license types by December 1, 2025. The Tennessee House passed it 68-21, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 1915. Counties and cities must verify that every public-benefit applicant age 18 or older is a United States citizen or legally present, and add a certification notice after the first form reprint or phone update after July 1, 2026. A final failed check ends recurring benefits, but a pending check alone cannot delay them. Agencies must also report people found not lawfully present to the state's centralized immigration enforcement division, and the attorney general may investigate local governments and withhold their state funds. The Tennessee House passed it 73-21, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 1915. Counties and cities must verify that every public-benefit applicant age 18 or older is a United States citizen or legally present, and add a certification notice after the first form reprint or phone update after July 1, 2026. A final failed check ends recurring benefits, but a pending check alone cannot delay them. Agencies must also report people found not lawfully present to the state's centralized immigration enforcement division, and the attorney general may investigate local governments and withhold their state funds. The Tennessee House passed it 73-21, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to accept the House's version of Senate Bill 1915, the final Senate vote on the bill. The law makes counties, cities, and towns check that each benefit applicant age 18 or older is a citizen or lawfully present. Local forms and automated phone systems must carry that notice after their first update following July 1, 2026. An agency may not delay a benefit only because the check is still pending. It must stop a recurring benefit once a final check shows the person is not a citizen or a qualified immigrant. Agencies must also report people who are not lawfully present and receive benefits to a state immigration enforcement office. An employee who knowingly fails to report commits a Class A misdemeanor. The attorney general may investigate local governments and withhold their state funding. The Senate agreed 24-6 and it became law as Public Chapter 1106.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against accepting the House's version of Senate Bill 1915, the final Senate vote on the bill. It extends Tennessee's citizenship checks for public benefits to counties, cities, and towns, for every applicant age 18 or older. Agencies must stop a recurring benefit once a final check shows the person is not a citizen or a qualified immigrant. They must report people who are not lawfully present and receive benefits to a state immigration enforcement office. An employee who knowingly fails to report commits a Class A misdemeanor. The attorney general may withhold state funding from local governments that do not comply. The Senate agreed 24-6 and it became law as Public Chapter 1106.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 670. It sorts isolated wetlands by quality and allows changes without permits, notice, or replacement work for any artificial wetland, low-quality sites up to one acre, and moderate sites up to one-quarter acre if pollution controls apply. Larger low- or moderate-quality sites up to two acres use one standard permit without some buffer, combined-impact, or protection rules; replacement is capped at 1:1 or 2:1. The Tennessee House passed it 71-21, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 670. It sorts isolated wetlands by quality and allows changes without permits, notice, or replacement work for any artificial wetland, low-quality sites up to one acre, and moderate sites up to one-quarter acre if pollution controls apply. Larger low- or moderate-quality sites up to two acres use one standard permit without some buffer, combined-impact, or protection rules; replacement is capped at 1:1 or 2:1. The Tennessee House passed it 71-21, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 2070. The Tennessee Energy Freedom Act blocks damages or court orders for coal, oil, or gas emissions unless federal environmental law was broken, and limits outside claims to products shipped there. It applies to past and out-of-state conduct, and a company reporting under ten percent of a China-India baseline is treated as having zero emissions. The Tennessee House passed it 69-18, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against House Bill 2070. The Tennessee Energy Freedom Act blocks damages or court orders for coal, oil, or gas emissions unless federal environmental law was broken, and limits outside claims to products shipped there. It applies to past and out-of-state conduct, and a company reporting under ten percent of a China-India baseline is treated as having zero emissions. The Tennessee House passed it 69-18, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 2348. High schools with 750 to 1,500 students need a full-time endorsed library specialist; schools below 750 need a part-time specialist or teacher coordinator, and staff must supervise an open library when no specialist is there. An advanced media-and-technology degree must count toward the specialist endorsement. The Tennessee House passed it 70-24, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 2348. High schools with 750 to 1,500 students need a full-time endorsed library specialist; schools below 750 need a part-time specialist or teacher coordinator, and staff must supervise an open library when no specialist is there. An advanced media-and-technology degree must count toward the specialist endorsement. The Tennessee House passed it 70-24, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 2040. Starting July 1, 2028, an owner above five percent generally cannot control a pharmacy plus both a health insurer and drug-benefit manager. Hospital pharmacies are not benefit managers, independent pharmacies keep mail, specialty, and delivery services, certain rare drugs are excluded, and a violating pharmacy may operate through December 31, 2028 during a real sale to an independent buyer. The Tennessee Senate passed it 24-9, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 2040. Starting July 1, 2028, an owner above five percent generally cannot control a pharmacy plus both a health insurer and drug-benefit manager. Hospital pharmacies are not benefit managers, independent pharmacies keep mail, specialty, and delivery services, certain rare drugs are excluded, and a violating pharmacy may operate through December 31, 2028 during a real sale to an independent buyer. The Tennessee Senate passed it 24-9, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 1360. It widens lawsuit protections from guns to listed weapons, armor, magazines, silencers, rapid-fire devices, sights, and accessories; lawful sales alone are not public nuisances, conspiracies, careless sales, or illegal business practices. Strong proof is required for careless sales and outside judgments, with triple damages and fees for failed enforcement, and local gun-rule control is further limited. The Tennessee House passed it 72-20, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 1360. It widens lawsuit protections from guns to listed weapons, armor, magazines, silencers, rapid-fire devices, sights, and accessories; lawful sales alone are not public nuisances, conspiracies, careless sales, or illegal business practices. Strong proof is required for careless sales and outside judgments, with triple damages and fees for failed enforcement, and local gun-rule control is further limited. The Tennessee House passed it 72-20, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1093. Machine gun now includes parts meant only to convert a gun; making, having, moving, fixing, or selling one rises from a Class E to a more serious Class C felony, and post-felony possession rules add ammunition. Aggravated assault by firing from a vehicle gets no probation and requires the full sentence with no early release. The Tennessee Senate passed it 23-8, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against House Bill 1093. Machine gun now includes parts meant only to convert a gun; making, having, moving, fixing, or selling one rises from a Class E to a more serious Class C felony, and post-felony possession rules add ammunition. Aggravated assault by firing from a vehicle gets no probation and requires the full sentence with no early release. The Tennessee Senate passed it 23-8, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for the Senate version of Senate Bill 336. It removed one certificate condition and replaced full child-support payment with twelve months of following all current orders, including overdue-payment orders. The Senate passed it 24-8; the final House rewrite instead changed the general restoration law, removed all court-cost payment, kept twelve-month child-support compliance, and became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against the Senate version of Senate Bill 336. It removed one certificate condition and replaced full child-support payment with twelve months of following all current orders, including overdue-payment orders. The Senate passed it 24-8; the final House rewrite instead changed the general restoration law, removed all court-cost payment, kept twelve-month child-support compliance, and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for the House rewrite of Senate Bill 336. It restores voting rights after a felony without requiring all court costs, but requires twelve months of following every child-support order, including overdue-payment orders. The Tennessee House passed it 64-24, the Senate agreed, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against the House rewrite of Senate Bill 336. It restores voting rights after a felony without requiring all court costs, but requires twelve months of following every child-support order, including overdue-payment orders. The Tennessee House passed it 64-24, the Senate agreed, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 2185. The voter-registration website may use the federal Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements program, which checks immigration status, when United States Citizenship and Immigration Services offers secure online access. The Tennessee House passed it 68-22, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against House Bill 2185. The voter-registration website may use the federal Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements program, which checks immigration status, when United States Citizenship and Immigration Services offers secure online access. The Tennessee House passed it 68-22, and it became law.
